classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Selection and approval are explicit operations with actor, reason, timestamp, evidence, and expected revision.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Transition requests carry actor, reason, time, idempotency, and expected revision, but selection/approval does not require evidence for the decision itself.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Add decision evidence references to selection/approval requests, validation, stable digests, and audit records with backward-compatible version handling.
testsRequired: selection and approval reject missing decision evidence
classifications.classificationEvidence: The current request type has no decision-evidence field; binding evidence cannot prove why a particular selection/approval was authorized.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate approval on retry.
classifications.claimedRootCause: The duplicate precheck is tenant/project/branch/key scoped but does not verify the owning binding set, component, target revision, or request digest.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Return replay only when owner and request digest match; reject same-key/different-owner or different-payload use deterministically.
testsRequired: cross-component key collision conflicts rather than suppressing work
classifications.classificationEvidence: server-repository.ts line 66 reads only the project-scoped key and returns duplicate without validating event ownership/content.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Audit records and current heads cannot disagree after a committed operation.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Immutable binding, audit, migration, and assessment inserts use onConflictDoNothing without comparing the existing row digest/payload before the head advances.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: On every immutable-row conflict, prove exact identity/digest equivalence or abort before publishing the head.
classifications.classificationEvidence: The four onConflictDoNothing calls are followed by head publication with no equivalence check.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Authorization is enforced at the service/API boundary, not only in UI code.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Mutation APIs derive tenant, project, actor, actor kind, session, and role from caller-controlled x-sirkit headers; domain capability checks trust that actor.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Adapt one trusted request-context interface backed by the product identity/session/project-membership authority and derive all four API scopes from it.
classifications.classificationEvidence: No user/session auth dependency, middleware, membership repository, or currentUser/getServerSession equivalent exists. engineering/authorization.ts is a domain capability map, while the only trusted bearer pattern is a machine worker secret and cannot identify human project membership.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Schema constraints prevent malformed or orphaned records where practical.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Selected revisions, migration candidates, assessments, positive revisions, lifecycle/state values, and relational references are enforced only by application convention.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: After an existing-data audit, add a new forward successor migration with practical foreign keys/checks and a quarantine/fail-closed plan for invalid rows; never rewrite 0022.
classifications.classificationEvidence: 0022 has not-null/unique indexes but no foreign keys or checks for the audited invariants, so a schema change is real; applied-state authority remains unknown.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Project passive policy is consumed as a versioned input, not as a hidden global default, and per-component exception is explicit and traceable.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Production Stage 3 constructs the resolver with the default disabled passive source and allowStage5PassivePolicy false; the real adapter is wired only in tests.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Create one production resolver composition root with durable B1/B4/B5/library inputs and use it for single, batch, and Stage 3 resolution.
classifications.classificationEvidence: app/api/pcb-sync/route.ts constructs FootprintResolutionService with only PostgresPhysicalBindingRepository; defaultSources installs a disabled passive hook.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: B1 and B2 use one consistent assembly-variant applicability contract, including global bindings represented by an empty variant list.
classifications.claimedRootCause: The engine treats an empty variant list as global while context validation and the mapping projector require explicit inclusion.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Centralize one variantApplies predicate and use it across repository/validation/engine/projector paths.
classifications.classificationEvidence: engine.ts explicitly allows length zero while validation.ts line 63 uses includes unconditionally; the contradiction is executable and not evidence-only.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Plan lifecycle survives application restart, and partial failure cannot leave plan, audit, and board state inconsistent.
classifications.claimedRootCause: apply commits lifecycle applying separately before the final board/plan/audit/replay/outbox transaction and has no stale-claim recovery after process death.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Remove the unsafe precommit publication or use a recoverable lease/state machine; keep final board/plan/audit/replay/outbox publication atomic.
testsRequired: fault before final commit leaves retryable plan
classifications.classificationEvidence: service.apply publishes applying through a separate repository commit; process death bypasses the catch/reset path.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Apply revalidates the exact plan against current schematic, binding, mapping, policy, library, and board revisions, and a stale or invalidated plan cannot apply.
classifications.claimedRootCause: The apply revalidation request sets requestedAt to plan.createdAt, so approval expiry and other time-sensitive state are evaluated at preflight time.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Use a trusted current apply time, re-fetch current authority heads, bind the result into revalidation, and reject clock regressions.
testsRequired: approval expires between preflight and apply
classifications.classificationEvidence: service.ts constructs revalidationRequest with requestedAt: plan.createdAt.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: No production PCB synchronization or board authority is stored only in a process-local Map, singleton, cache, or browser state.
classifications.claimedRootCause: The shipping editor directly builds/mutates a board through legacy sync and saves board/current-project/sync-hash authority in browser localStorage beside the durable B3 API.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Switch the existing editor call to a durable B3 client contract, treat local data only as explicit migration/cache state, and retain legacy sync only as a non-authoritative importer.
testsRequired: editor sync uses durable preflight/apply boundary
local copy cannot outrank server revision
classifications.classificationEvidence: PcbEditor.tsx imports and calls syncFromSchematic at line 353 and imports load/saveCurrentBoard from board-persistence; the current function signature lacks trusted project/actor/expected-board revision, so a safe durable switch cannot be hidden entirely inside B1-B6.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Verification results are durable, immutable or revisioned, and evidence-bound.
classifications.claimedRootCause: rememberResult writes the process-local Map before awaiting durable resultStore.put, so failed persistence leaves consumable memory-only state.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Persist first, populate only a bounded read-through cache after success, and reload/verify the durable digest before authoritative mutation.
testsRequired: durable put failure leaves no cache
classifications.classificationEvidence: service.ts line 33 executes results.set before await resultStore.put and later mutation reads the map.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: A verified mapping projects into B1 without creating competing authorities, and superseding or revoking it durably and recoverably invalidates every dependent resolver result and PCB preflight plan.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Owner commit reports success while projection and invalidation are separate unordered outbox effects with no completion barrier; mapping approval also directly creates an approved B1 successor.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Add explicit pending/applied/failed projection status, event dependency/ordering, idempotent completion, reconciled invalidation outcome, and a B1 decision contract that does not equate mapping verification with physical-binding approval.
testsRequired: mapping approval does not silently approve B1
classifications.classificationEvidence: durable.ts emits mapping.stage1-project and mapping.invalidate independently; service returns a projected reference immediately and stores stage3PlansStaled as zero.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Per-component exception is an explicit authoritative operation, not an incidental field edit.
classifications.claimedRootCause: assign_profile is accepted and persisted, but the evaluator handles only opt_out and require_exact_part and silently falls through to generic rules.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Implement exact pinned-profile behavior or reject assign_profile until its complete authority fields are present; never silently fall through.
classifications.classificationEvidence: evaluator.ts branches for opt_out and require_exact_part only, despite types/service accepting assign_profile.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Exception approval records actor, reason, component, chosen package or footprint, evidence, expected policy, context and component revision, and idempotency key, and applies only to its intended project/component/revision scope.
classifications.claimedRootCause: The decision lacks pinned context/component/profile/footprint revisions and complete evidence; expected revision protects only the policy head.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Make the exception a revision-bound decision containing component fact digest, context revision, chosen profile/package/footprint identity and revision, evidence, actor/reason/time, and expected heads.
classifications.classificationEvidence: The current exception and mutation types carry component/variant and policy revision but no pinned fact/context/profile/footprint revision set.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Removal or supersession of an exception cannot leave stale ready state.
classifications.claimedRootCause: No revoke/remove/supersede exception operation exists; edit replaces by ID but always persists approved state.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Add revision-checked revoke/supersede operations, audit action, durable invalidation, and readiness transition.
classifications.classificationEvidence: service.ts exposes applyApprovedException only and always sets state approved; the API has no explicit exception revocation action.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Outbox events have durable identity, owner revision, event type and version, payload digest, creation state, attempt count, next-attempt time, and terminal state.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Events contain topic/payload/retry state but no explicit owner aggregate type/key/revision or event schema version separate from convention.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Add durable owner and event-version fields in one forward migration, bind them into event identity/digest, validate dispatch, and backfill existing pending events safely.
classifications.classificationEvidence: The TypeScript and 0023 table omit owner aggregate/revision and event version; a real schema successor is required, but applied-state authority is unknown.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Durable aggregate identity and every head/history/CAS lookup enforce tenant, project, and branch isolation rather than relying on caller key convention.
classifications.claimedRootCause: Head/record uniqueness and lookups use aggregate type/key only; tenant/project/branch columns exist but are not part of the generic identity contract.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Make scope mandatory in identity/lookups/CAS and add scoped unique/index constraints through a forward migration with collision audit.
testsRequired: same aggregate key in two tenants remains isolated
classifications.classificationEvidence: schema.ts unique indexes and server-repository loadHead/history omit scope even though scope columns are present.

classifications.exactOriginalRequirement: Migration application must detect an incompatible pre-existing durable-workflow object rather than silently treating it as the intended 0023 shape.
classifications.claimedRootCause: CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS could accept a same-named incompatible object if deployment state is already drifted.
classifications.claimedMinimumRepair: Qualify clean, compatible-existing, and incompatible-existing database states and require schema-shape verification/forward-fix procedure; do not rewrite 0023.
classifications.classificationEvidence: The journal is the migration-application authority and current table definitions are structurally coherent. IF NOT EXISTS is dangerous only under pre-existing drift; proving detection and recovery is an isolated PostgreSQL Q2/Q4 obligation. Rewriting historical 0023 would be less safe.

gapDependencies.reason: Replay collision semantics and immutable-row collision handling must agree.
Do not enable the passive candidate source while assign_profile silently falls through.
Production resolver inputs require revision-complete exception decisions.
Production resolver must observe exception revocation/supersession.
Apply revalidation must include the final production resolver composition.
The editor must consume a restart-safe B3 apply lifecycle.
The durable editor path must use current-time revalidation.
A durable client path requires trusted request context.
Projection cannot consume a pre-durable verification result.
Effect completion needs explicit owner revision and event version.
Projection/invalidation status must be tenant/project scoped.
assign_profile is safe only with a pinned profile/context/component decision.
Revocation invalidation requires the repaired outbox contract.
Forward migration authority and scoped durable identity must be established first.

app/lib/pcb-sync/authorization.ts validates a supplied actor and plan scope

authenticationDecision.errorModel: domain APIs already use stable unauthorized/scope-mismatch codes; the new adapter must preserve those codes without trusting request headers
authenticationDecision.auditIdentityRepresentation: EngineeringActor with actorId, actorKind, sessionId, role and optional delegation fields
testUtilities: existing API handler tests construct x-sirkit headers
worker-secret tests can be reused only for machine endpoints
authenticationDecision.selectedApproach: Define a minimal TrustedEngineeringRequestContextProvider interface returning verified tenant/project/branch membership plus EngineeringActor. Do not implement an identity provider inside footprint remediation. Adapt the four B1-B5 scope modules only after the product supplies a real provider.
authenticationDecision.whyWorkerSecretIsInsufficient: It authenticates a machine worker only and contains no human identity, project membership, or role authority.

migrationDecision.journalState: 0006 through 0023 exist once and are strictly ordered; latest verified identifier is 0023
migrationDecision.schemaState: 0022 and 0023 match current TypeScript table shape, but required B1 constraints and B6 owner/scoped identity fields are absent
migrationDecision.toolingState: package.json exposes drizzle-kit generate and push, but no authoritative migrate/deploy script or deployment-state record
migrationDecision.localStateEvidence: An .env.local name exists but values were not read and no database was contacted; it is not safe applied-state authority
migrationDecision.historyRule: Never edit 0022 or 0023. Use forward successors only.
migrationDecision.firstGate: R03-B06 must prove an isolated disposable database or obtain deployment migration inventory before changing schema/journal; unknown deployment history does not block code-only batches B01-B05.
migrationDecision.r04Obligation: Apply the full chain cleanly and through predecessor upgrade/failure scenarios after all implementation batches.

batches.title: B1 decision and repository integrity
batches.purpose: Close decision-evidence, replay-identity, and immutable-row collision defects in the physical-binding authority without schema changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Selection/approval cannot omit decision evidence.
Replay returns only an identical committed request.
No conflicting immutable row can coexist with a newly published head.
All R03-attributable changes remain within budget.

batches.title: B3 apply-time and lifecycle safety
batches.purpose: Make plan apply retryable across interruption and revalidate against current time/current authority without changing browser integration.
tests: fault after apply starts but before final commit
acceptanceCriteria: No plan can be stranded in applying without a deterministic recovery path.
Apply uses trusted current time and current authority inputs.
Board/plan/audit/replay publication remains one durable commit.

batches.title: B4 durable-first verification result
batches.purpose: Remove process-local mapping verification authority by making durable persistence precede any cache visibility.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed durable write leaves no usable in-memory result.
Authoritative mutation verifies the durable result digest.

batches.title: B5 revision-complete exception lifecycle
batches.purpose: Implement safe assign_profile semantics, revision-complete exception decisions, and explicit revoke/supersede behavior.
batches.migration: none; durable JSON records receive a versioned compatible contract
acceptanceCriteria: No accepted exception action silently falls through.
Every decision is bound to exact component/context/profile authority.
Revocation creates an auditable successor and durable invalidation intent.

batches.title: B2 production policy composition and variant contract
batches.purpose: Use one versioned passive-policy source in production resolution and one global/exact variant predicate everywhere.
tests: production composition uses durable passive source
policy/exception revision appears in dependency digest
acceptanceCriteria: Production and tests use the same resolver inputs.
No passive policy is a hidden global default.
Global variant semantics are identical in B1/B2/B4 consumers.

batches.title: B6 scoped durable workflow and versioned outbox
batches.purpose: Resolve migration authority, then enforce scoped aggregate identity and explicit versioned owner-bound outbox events in the shared primitive and B3-B5 adapters.
batches.migration: proposed successor 0024 only after the batch's isolated applied-state gate
acceptanceCriteria: Migration authority is documented before journal change.
No unscoped production B1-B5 lookup remains.
Every outbox event identifies owner revision and event version.
Historical 0022/0023 remain byte-identical.

batches.title: B1 forward relational integrity
batches.purpose: Add practical B1 orphan/revision/state constraints using a forward successor after B6 migration authority is established.
acceptanceCriteria: Practical relational invariants are database enforced.
Invalid existing rows fail a documented preflight rather than being silently dropped.
Historical migrations remain unchanged.

batches.title: B4/B5 projection and invalidation convergence
batches.purpose: Make mapping projection and mapping/passive plan invalidation ordered, observable, idempotent, and readiness-gated on completion.
tests: projection or invalidation terminal failure remains not-ready
mapping approval distinct from B1 approval
acceptanceCriteria: Owner success is not readiness success until required effects complete.
B4 verification cannot silently become B1 physical approval.
Every failed effect is durable, observable, and retryable or terminal.

batches.title: Trusted engineering request context integration
batches.purpose: Integrate B1/B3/B4/B5 mutation APIs with a real product-supplied identity/session/project-membership authority without inventing one.
batches.migration: none unless the separately supplied platform membership authority explicitly requires one outside this remediation
tests: stable audit actor derived from trusted context
acceptanceCriteria: A real provider is identified before editing.
Request bodies/headers cannot assert trusted actor, role, tenant, or membership.
All four mutation API families fail closed without verified context.

batches.title: Frozen B7 contract compatibility only
batches.purpose: Update only proven B7 consumers for repaired B1/B3/B5/B6 contracts and replace legacy browser PCB authority; add no queue feature or UI redesign.
tests: local board cannot outrank server revision
acceptanceCriteria: Changes are limited to compile/behavior compatibility proved above.
No new queue action, workbench UX, bulk behavior, or Stage 7 resync feature is added.
Legacy local state is explicit import/cache only.
Frozen Stage 6 focused compilation/tests pass.

unresolvedUserDecisions.question: Which existing external product identity/session/project-membership authority must implement TrustedEngineeringRequestContextProvider?
unresolvedUserDecisions.whyMaterial: The repository contains no human auth or membership authority; choosing or creating one changes the platform security boundary and cannot be inferred from worker-secret or caller-header patterns.

unresolvedUserDecisions.question: Provide authoritative applied-migration inventory for 0022/0023, or approve an isolated-database-first forward-only decision gate before 0024/0025 are added.
unresolvedUserDecisions.whyMaterial: The journal is present but no migrate/deploy script, deployment record, or safe database state proves what has been applied.
